fact: Global cooling and sea-level drop triggered the second largest mass extinction; ~85% of marine species disappeared.
Multi-phase prolonged extinction, collapse of coral reef ecosystems, many invertebrates vanished.
The worst extinction event in Earth history, over 90% marine and 70% terrestrial species died, known as "The Great Dying".
places: Russia; South Africa; Changxing Zhejiang China

fact: Mass volcanic activity caused greenhouse warming, many land and marine species extinct, empty niches allowed dinosaurs to rise.
Asteroid impact plus volcanic activity killed non-avian dinosaurs and ammonites; mammals began to diversify.
Late-Cambrian small extinction event, many early trilobite families disappeared, marine faunas restructured.
Regional-scale marine extinction, reef-building archaeocyathids completely vanished from global oceans.
Pre-cursor mass extinction before end-Permian event, severe marine biodiversity loss, many reef organisms died out.
Minor but widespread extinction, many Jurassic marine reptiles and bivalve species disappeared.
Grande Coupure major turnover event, dramatic global cooling, many European mammals went extinct.
Messinian salinity crisis precursor extinction; many shallow-marine species vanished as Mediterranean began to dry.
Late Quaternary megafauna extinction; large ice-age mammals disappeared across most continents, mixed climate-human drivers.
names: mammoth; woolly rhinoceros; giant ground sloth
